definition: the flat display surface of a phone, computer, or tablet.
example: She wiped the screen before starting the video call.
originNote: from a word meaning shield or protection
spellingTip: The long ee sound is written with double e.

definition: a program used to view websites on the internet.
example: Open your browser and type in the web address.
originNote: related to browsing or looking around
spellingTip: Remember brow like eyebrow, then add ser.

definition: a set of keys used to enter letters and commands into a device.
example: He spilled water near the keyboard by accident.
spellingTip: Key keeps the ey spelling for the long e sound.

definition: a device that stores energy to power electronic equipment.
example: My tablet stopped working because the battery was flat.
originNote: from a word linked to beating or striking
spellingTip: Double t comes before the ery ending.

definition: a piece of written or spoken communication sent electronically.
example: I sent a message to confirm the meeting time.
originNote: from a word for communication sent by messenger
spellingTip: It ends with age, not idge.

definition: using electronic signals or computer technology.
example: The library now keeps a digital record of every loan.
originNote: from digitus meaning finger or number
spellingTip: The soft g sounds like j before i.

definition: a piece of electronic equipment made for a particular purpose.
example: Each student brought a device for the coding lesson.
originNote: from a word meaning plan or design
spellingTip: The ending is vice with a c, not s.

definition: the programs and data used by a computer.
example: The new software helps us edit photos more quickly.
spellingTip: Ware is the same spelling as in hardware.

example: We connected the printer to the wireless network.
spellingTip: Keep the final e in wire before adding less.

definition: a set of related pages on the internet.
example: Our class website has the homework and timetable.
spellingTip: Site uses i before t, not website with y.

definition: the global system of connected computer networks.
example: The internet was slow during the storm.
spellingTip: Inter is a common prefix meaning between.

definition: a set of coded instructions that tells a computer what to do.
example: She wrote a simple program to sort the numbers.
originNote: from a root meaning something written beforehand
spellingTip: Technology uses program, not the longer programme here.

definition: a group of connected computers or devices that share information.
example: The whole network went down after lunch.
spellingTip: Work keeps the or spelling, not er.

definition: a device with moving or electronic parts that performs a task.
example: The washing machine stopped halfway through the cycle.
originNote: from a word meaning device or contrivance
spellingTip: Ch here sounds like sh in machine.

definition: a device used to take photographs or record video.
example: He packed a camera for the excursion.
originNote: from camera meaning chamber or room
spellingTip: The middle sound is er, not ar.

definition: a device used to play electronic games.
example: My brother saved up for a new console.
originNote: from a word for a supporting structure
spellingTip: Sole sounds like sohl and ends with e.

definition: a machine that produces words or pictures on paper.
example: The printer ran out of ink during class.
originNote: from a root meaning press or mark
spellingTip: Print stays whole before adding er.

definition: a transmission that carries information between devices.
example: There was no signal in the underground station.
originNote: from signum meaning mark or sign
spellingTip: The end is nal, not nell.
